h: Roman Forts, Village Pubs and Big Skies
p: Matfen sits in a part of Northumberland where history is never far away, and it pays to plan a couple of stops around your treetop session. Chesters Roman Fort, near Chollerford, is a brilliant place to get a feel for life on Hadrian's Wall, with the remains of a bath house down by the River North Tyne. Corbridge Roman Town is close too, and Corbridge village itself is a lovely little place for a wander, with independent shops and spots for a cuppa.

Belsay Hall, Castle and Gardens, looked after by English Heritage, is also within easy reach. It mixes a medieval castle, a grand Greek-style hall and quarry gardens that feel almost tropical in summer, so it's a cracking contrast to an afternoon in the woods.

On the day, plan for the treetop course to take a couple of hours, and remember that rural roads around here can be slower going than you'd expect. Fuel up before you leave town, as there aren't many shops on the way, and keep water and snacks in the car.

Northumberland weather can be bracing even in summer, so pack a warm layer and a waterproof that folds small. Gloves are a good idea for anyone with soft hands, and a hat that won't blow off on the zip wires is a bonus.
Being west of Newcastle, Matfen also works well as a morning trip from the city, leaving plenty of time to head back for an evening on the Quayside.
